title: The Two-Headed Bird
text:
By a lake there lived a strange bird called a Bharunda. It had one body and one stomach, but two necks and two heads.

One day, as the bird walked along the shore, one of its heads came upon a fruit that had washed up on the bank. It tasted wonderful, sweet as nectar, and the head ate it all. The second head asked for a taste. The first refused. They shared one stomach, it said, so what difference did it make which mouth ate the fruit?

The second head said nothing, but it brooded. Some days later it found a poisonous fruit. The first head saw it and begged it not to eat, since the poison would kill them both. The second head reminded it of the nectar fruit and ate the poison anyway.

The poison went into the stomach they shared, and the bird died.
lesson: Members of a team who share one fate cannot win by spiting each other. Small slights left unresolved can grow into revenge that ruins everyone.
